newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London becalmed in cautious Europe.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London becalmed in cautious Europe.

text.p: U.S. shares were little changed in quiet trade on Thursday as many European investors continued to wonder whether or not Wall Street's rally over the past two weeks could be sustained.
"Nobody knows which way to jump. The Dow has come back too fast and people think it could be heading for another fall," one dealer said.
"This rally has been on the back of good earnings news but once that stops, the market is going to start worrying about interest rates again."

The Dow Industrials Average, which since hitting a 1997 low of 6,391.69 on April 11 had clawed back over 440 points or nearly two-thirds of a 700 point drop, finished 20.87 points down to 6,812.72 on Wednesday.
Technical analysts said the Dow could still push higher for a few more days but would find strong resistance at around 6,880-6,900.
"What we've seen over the past week is just a technical rally from an overbought position," said Richard Marshall, chartist at Investment Research of Cambridge Ltd.
Marshall said the Dow's two-week surge had not been supported by either market breadth or bond yields.
"What we haven't got is confirmation from the bond market or the advance/decline indicator. They haven't moved very far at all so they are not confirming the rally," Marshall said.

Marshall noted that the yield on the 30-year long bond had stubbornly stayed well above the 7.00 percent level and could still test resistance at 7.20 in the near-term."Unless these bonds pick up from here, I don't expect the Dow to go up much further at the present."
The long bond yield stood at 7.08 percent by 1025 GMT, while the June T-bond was up 2/32 to 107-25/32.
Over the next few months, Marshall thought the Dow would trade in a range between 6,400 to 6,900 before heading higher sometime in mid-summer.

"The bull trend has not changed," but cautioned that a breach of the 6,200 level could signal the end of the Dow's uptrend. If we fall below that and stay below I would start to get worried," Marshall said.
IBM, which rose $2-3/8 on Wednesday, was up $1 to $143-3/8 after it reported first-quarter earnings per share, matching the very highest of Wall Street estimates.
Halliburton Co added $1/8 to $74, after the company on Wednesday reported first quarter earnings of $0.65 a share versus a First Call mean estimate of $0.63 per share.
The June S&P 500 futures contract was up 0.45 to 780.65.
